I don't have access to your actual dashboards or monitoring systems, so I can't independently verify the data — but the detail you raised yourself is the one I'd stop on before posting all-clear.

**The EU routing cluster gap is the real risk here.** If the Checkout Errors dashboard was built before last month's migration and doesn't ingest metrics from the new routing cluster, "flat at zero for 25 minutes" doesn't mean checkout is healthy — it could mean the dashboard simply isn't seeing a chunk of production traffic. That's a materially different conclusion than "the revert worked," and it's exactly the kind of gap that looks fine right up until someone checks EU-specific numbers tomorrow.

Before posting the all-clear, I'd want one concrete fact, not an inference: does that dashboard's query/data source explicitly include the new EU cluster? If you're not sure, that's answerable in a couple minutes by either checking the dashboard's underlying query/service list, or pulling error rate directly from the EU cluster's own metrics.

Given the 20-minute clock, my suggestion: don't let the all-hands drive the timeline on this one specific check. Two options that don't require rushing —
- Quick verify now (check the dashboard config or hit EU error metrics directly) — if EU is covered and clean, close it with confidence.
- If you can't verify in time, post an update instead of an all-clear: "error rate back to baseline since config revert at 2:35, confirming coverage across EU cluster before formal close" — then close it properly after the all-hands.

The revert-then-drop correlation is a reasonable working hypothesis for root cause, but I'd hold the "confirmed" language until the coverage question is answered — that's the one gap between "looks resolved" and "is resolved."
